chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

That Asma' bint Umays gave birth to Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered her, when she intended to enter the state of Ihram from Dhu al-Hulayfa, to stuff herself with cotton and rags and to begin with Hajj. So when they arrived in Mecca and had performed the rituals, and eighteen days had passed for her, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered her to perform Tawaf by the House and to pray, and the blood had not ceased from her, so she did that.

key_terms.الْإِحْرَام: The state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.الْكُرْسُف: Cotton or soft cloth used for absorption

ai.seo_question: Can a woman perform Tawaf and pray during Hajj while still in post-childbirth bleeding?
ai.summary: This foundational hadith from al-Kafi records the Prophet Muhammad’s directive to Asma’ bint Umays, mother of Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, allowing her to perform Tawaf and Salat during Hajj despite persistent post-childbirth bleeding (nifas) for eighteen days. It establishes the principle that the absence of blood cessation does not invalidate the core pillars of Hajj, a ruling widely cited by Shia jurists to distinguish between ritual purity requirements for prayer versus pilgrimage. The narration highlights the practical flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding women's ritual status during major religious obligations.
